paragraphs.notes: Continuous run-on substituent enumeration; the page carries no [00NN] paragraph marker of any kind, and the body opens mid-list with a lowercase word ('alkinyloxycarbonylamino'), so it is the continuation of the list running from the previous page and it continues onto the next. TRANSCRIPTION CONVENTION: the printed line breaks are not reproduced. Lines are joined with a single space, except where a line ends in a hyphen, where the next line is joined with no space so the hyphenated term is restored. Four such breaks occur: '...-N-alkyl-' / 'amino' three times, and 'Cyclo-' / 'alkenylalkinyloxycarbonyl-...' once. In the first three the hyphen is unambiguously part of the term '-N-alkyl-amino'. In the fourth it is NOT determinable from the page whether the hyphen in 'Cyclo-alkenylalkinyloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' is a real hyphen or a typographic line-break hyphen; it is kept as printed and not resolved. SPELLING AS PRINTED, NOT CORRECTED: several terms print 'alkiny' where the parallel terms print 'alkinyl' - 'Heteroarylalkinyoxycarbonylamino', 'Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonylamino', 'Arylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy', 'Heteroarylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy', 'Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy', 'Arylalkinyoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino', 'Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino'. These are verified at magnification and transcribed verbatim per rule 1. Likewise 'Heterocyclylalkenyloxycarbonyl-amino' prints without the '-N-alkyl' that every neighbouring term in that run carries, and 'Alkoxycarbonylamino' / 'Alkenyloxycarbonylamino' appear a second time in the -N-alkyl-amino run without the '-N-alkyl' infix. Recorded as printed; not normalised. LANGUAGE: the page is German (Alkinyl, Halogenalkyl, Cycloalkenyl), so 'zh' holds the German as printed per the run convention. The 'en' field maps the German substituent nomenclature to English (Alkinyl -> alkynyl, Halogen- -> halo-) term for term, in the same order and with the same count; it is a nomenclature mapping, not prose translation, and the as-printed 'alkiny' truncations above are carried through as 'alkyn' rather than silently repaired.
